# Ten Songs of Tagore, In Data (Swaralipi Corpus v0.1)

> An openly licensed, machine-readable corpus of Rabindrasangeet (Tagore song) notation. Ten songs
> encoded from akarmatrik swaralipi — the Bengali notation system — into a symbolic JSON format
> that preserves swara, saptak, matra-fraction timing, taal cycles and Bengali lyric alignment.
> To our knowledge the first such dataset to exist under an open licence.

Compositions by Rabindranath Tagore (1861-1941), public domain in India since 2002.
Data: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT. Maintained by Indranil (Neel) Banerjee.

## What is in it
- 10 songs, 214 notated lines, 2,543 matra-cells, 3,195 note-units
- Taals covered: ektaal (12), dadra (6), kaharba (8), tintal (16), khemta (6), plus one
  talamukta (free-rhythm) song
- Derived MIDI and MusicXML; reference audio synthesized from the notation itself, not recorded
- Per-song provenance: witness archive, URL, retrieval date, confidence level
- 3 of 10 songs verified matra-by-matra against scans of the printed Swarabitan

## Notable findings
- পুরানো সেই দিনের কথা: 94.1% of its notes are the Bhupali pentatonic, the rest seven Ni and one
  Ma — matching the printed raga name "Mishra (mixed) Bhupali", measured before that name was known
- ভালোবেসে সখী is talamukta, not dadra: the printed page carries no taal header and no vibhag bars
- Across the corpus, Pa falls on sam (beat one) nearly twice as often as Sa
